record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.context_brief: Rational Kronecker factors for commuting polynomials
record.original_question: Suppose p1, ..., pℓ are rationally independent integer polynomials and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure-preserving transformations. Are the rational Kronecker factors Krat(T1), ..., Krat(Tℓ) characteristic for the polynomial averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{p1(n)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}fℓ?

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Suppose that the polynomials p1, . . . , p` ∈ Z[t] are rationally independent. Show that Krat(T1), . . . , Krat(T`) are characteristic factors for the averages (17).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\dots,T_\ell\colon X\to X$ be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations. For a measure-preserving transformation $T$ on $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$, the rational Kronecker factor $K_{\mathrm{rat}}(T)$ is the sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\mathcal{B}$ generated by all measurable functions $f\in L^2(\mu)$ such that $Tf = e^{2\pi i \alpha} f$ for some rational number $\alpha\in\mathbb{Q}$ (equivalently, the factor spanned by eigenfunctions of $T$ with roots of unity as eigenvalues).

Let $p_1,\dots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be integer polynomials that are rationally independent, meaning that the polynomials $p_1,\dots,p_\ell$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$ (no nontrivial rational linear combination of them is the zero polynomial, and more generally none is constant).

A collection of factors $\mathcal{Y}_1,\dots,\mathcal{Y}_\ell$ of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T_1,\dots,T_\ell)$ is called characteristic for the multiple polynomial average
$$A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell) \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} (T_1^{p_1(n)} f_1)\cdots (T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)} f_\ell)$$
if, for all $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\bigl\|A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell) - A_N(\mathbb{E}(f_1\mid\mathcal{Y}_1),\dots,\mathbb{E}(f_\ell\mid\mathcal{Y}_\ell))\bigr\|_{L^2(\mu)} = 0.$$

Prove or disprove: for every such system and every choice of rationally independent $p_1,\dots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$, the rational Kronecker factors $K_{\mathrm{rat}}(T_1),\dots,K_{\mathrm{rat}}(T_\ell)$ are characteristic for the averages $A_N(f_1,\dots,f_\ell)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Frantzikinakis and Kuca (e.g., "Joint ergodicity for commuting transformations and applications to polynomial sequences", 2022/2023) establishes that, under linear/rational independence of the integer polynomials, the rational Kronecker factors of commuting measure-preserving transformations are characteristic for the corresponding multiple polynomial averages, and derive Khintchine-type lower bounds. This appears to substantially settle the problem in the affirmative under the stated rational independence hypothesis, though full equivalence with the original formulation should be checked carefully.

status_evidence.title: Joint ergodicity for commuting transformations and applications to polynomial sequences
status_evidence.snippet: when the polynomials are linearly independent, we show that the rational Kronecker factor is characteristic and deduce Khintchine-type lower bounds for the related multiple recurrence problem
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that rational Kronecker factors are characteristic for polynomial multiple averages with commuting transformations under linear independence of the polynomials.

status_evidence.title: Joint ergodicity of sequences
status_evidence.snippet: rational Kronecker factors ... characteristic ... polynomial averages
status_evidence.claim: Related results on joint ergodicity and characteristic factors for polynomial sequences in commuting setups.
